title: Priority Mosaic: scenario-driven RICE + latency-cost surface simulator
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, reproducible prioritization framework (Priority Mosaic) that augments classic RICE scores with multi-dimensional cost and latency surfaces, scenario-driven simulations, and sensitivity visualizations so PMs can make trade-offs across throughput, latency SLOs, and unit economics.

Why now: The product and engineering teams need a repeatable rubric that captures both product value signals (reach/impact, confidence) and operational constraints (token cost, added latency, required GPU capacity). Existing RICE sheets miss non-linearities introduced by batching, prefix caching, and model variant fallbacks. Priority Mosaic encodes those effects as surfaces and runs scenario sims to produce robust ranking buckets rather than brittle single-point scores.

Approach summary:
- Inputs: per-initiative estimated daily requests, average tokens per request, target latency SLOs (p50/p95), model family (e.g., medium/gpt-large/quantized), cacheable prefix fraction, and relative importance (impact/confidence).
- Surface modeling: build two continuous surfaces: cost-per-1000-reqs and p95-latency as functions of batch size and cache hit rate for each model variant. Surfaces combine runtime profiles (from ENG telemetry) and kernel/quantization profiles.
- Scenario simulation: Monte Carlo over traffic mix (3-5 traffic scenarios: baseline, surge, enterprise-peak), sampling cache hit & batch distributions, and modeling automatic fallbacks (e.g., to cheaper quantized model or regional failover). For each initiative simulate 1k draws to estimate distribution of cost delta, latency breach probability, and throughput headroom.
- Scoring fusion: compute a composite score by fusing R, I, C, E where C (cost) is drawn from the simulated cost distribution (use median for point ranking and tail metrics for risk buckets) and E (effort) incorporates estimated engineering complexity and rollout risk. Provide rank buckets (A/B/C) and recommended experiments/guardrails for A items with non-trivial tail risk.
- Visual output: an interactive "mosaic" heatmap—rows=initiatives, columns=scenarios, cell shows median cost delta and p95-breach probability; click to expand to sensitivity tornado plots and a small decision card (recommended action, guardrail, required telemetry).

Deliverables:
1) Prototype Jupyter notebook that ingests initiative CSV and runtime profiles and outputs ranked buckets + per-initiative simulation report.
2) Mockup mosaic dashboard (Figma link) and a simple HTML export for PMs.
3) Integration plan to export the top-20 ranked items into the roadmap tracker and attach simulation artifacts.
4) Guidance doc: how to set input priors, conservative defaults, and escalation rules when tail risk > 10%.

Success criteria: framework used by at least two PMs during cycle planning, and PMs report that simulation results changed the ordering for >=2 initiatives compared to naive RICE.

Produce ranked bucket output (A/B/C) and per-initiative report PDF for top-20 items
Mosaic mockup completed and reviewed by Design with annotated interactions
ENG provides runtime profile snapshots (cost/latency by batch/cache) for three representative models
